sentences.chinese: 向雄 段灼 閻纘
sentences.literal: Xiang Xiong; Duan Zhuo; Yan Zuan.
sentences.idiomatic: Biographies of Xiang Xiong, Duan Zhuo, and Yan Zuan.

sentences.chinese: 向雄，字茂伯，河內山陽人也。
sentences.literal: Xiang Xiong, courtesy Maobo, was a man of Shanyang in Hanoi commandery.
sentences.idiomatic: Xiang Xiong, courtesy name Maobo, came from Shanyang in Hanoi.

sentences.chinese: 父韶，彭城太守。
sentences.literal: His father Xiang Shao was Grand Administrator of Pengcheng.
sentences.idiomatic: His father, Xiang Shao, had served as governor of Pengcheng.

sentences.chinese: 雄初仕郡為主簿，事太守王經。
sentences.literal: At first Xiong served the commandery as chief clerk and attended Grand Administrator Wang Jing.
sentences.idiomatic: Xiang Xiong began his career as chief clerk of the commandery under Prefect Wang Jing.

sentences.chinese: 及經之死也，雄哭之盡哀，市人咸為之悲。
sentences.literal: When it came to Jing's death, Xiong wept for him with complete grief; market people all for it felt sorrow.
sentences.idiomatic: When Wang Jing was put to death, Xiang Xiong mourned him bitterly, and the crowds at the execution ground wept with him.

sentences.chinese: 後太守劉毅嘗以非罪笞雄，及吳奮代毅為太守，又以少譴系雄於獄。
sentences.literal: Later Grand Administrator Liu Yi once for no real crime flogged Xiong; when Wu Fen replaced Yi as grand administrator, again for a slight fault he bound Xiong in prison.
sentences.idiomatic: Later, Prefect Liu Yi had him flogged without real cause; when Wu Fen succeeded Liu Yi, he jailed Xiang Xiong over a minor reprimand.

sentences.chinese: 司隸鐘會於獄中辟雄為都官從事，會死無人殯斂，雄迎喪而葬之。
sentences.literal: Metropolitan Governor Zhong Hui from within prison summoned Xiong as clerk for capital affairs; when Hui died none laid him out, and Xiong received the corpse and buried it.
sentences.idiomatic: Metropolitan Commissioner Zhong Hui recruited him from jail as an aide in judicial affairs; after Zhong Hui died with no one to lay him out, Xiang Xiong claimed the body and gave him burial.

sentences.chinese: 文帝召雄而責之曰：「往者王經之死，卿哭王經於東市，我不問也。
sentences.literal: King Wen summoned Xiong and reproached him, saying: When formerly Wang Jing died, you wept for Wang Jing at the eastern market; I did not inquire.
sentences.idiomatic: King Wen summoned Xiang Xiong and rebuked him: When Wang Jing died, you mourned him publicly at the eastern market; I let that pass.

sentences.chinese: 今鐘會躬為叛逆，又輒收葬，若復相容，其如王法何！
sentences.literal: Now Zhong Hui personally was a rebel; again you presumptuously gathered and buried him. If again we tolerate one another, what of royal law!
sentences.idiomatic: Zhong Hui turned traitor with his own hands, yet you took it on yourself to bury him. If such behavior keeps getting a pass, what becomes of the law?

sentences.chinese: 」雄曰：「昔者先王掩骼埋胔，仁流朽骨，當時豈先卜其功罪而後葬之哉！
sentences.literal: Xiong said: Of old the former kings covered bones and buried flesh left exposed; benevolence reached rotten bones. In that age did they first divine merit and guilt and afterward bury them!
sentences.idiomatic: Xiang Xiong replied: The kings of old gathered exposed bones and buried the dead; their kindness extended even to decayed remains. Did they first weigh each person's guilt or merit before granting burial?

sentences.chinese: 今王誅既加，於法已備。
sentences.literal: Now kingly punishment already has been applied; in law it is already complete.
sentences.idiomatic: Royal justice has already been carried out; the sentence under law is finished.

sentences.chinese: 雄感義收葬，教亦無闕。
sentences.literal: Xiong, moved by duty, gathered and buried; in instruction also there is no lack.
sentences.idiomatic: I buried him out of a sense of moral duty, and that breaks no principle of moral teaching.

sentences.chinese: 法立於上，教弘於下，何必使雄違生背死以立于時！
sentences.literal: Law is set above; instruction spreads below—why must one make Xiong violate the living and turn against the dead so as to stand in the age!
sentences.idiomatic: Law comes from above and moral teaching spreads below; why must you force me to dishonor the living and betray the dead just to cut a figure in this world?

sentences.chinese: 殿下仇枯骨而捐之中野，為將來仁賢之資，不亦惜乎！
sentences.literal: Your Highness hates dry bones and casts them away in the open wild—material for later humane and worthy men—is it not regrettable!
sentences.idiomatic: If Your Highness leaves dried bones as enemies and abandons them in the wilderness, you supply posterity's humane and worthy men with a sad precedent—is that not a pity?

sentences.chinese: 」帝甚悅，與談宴而遣之。
sentences.literal: The king greatly delighted; with him he conversed at banquet and sent him away.
sentences.idiomatic: The king was greatly pleased, talked with him over a feast, and dismissed him.

sentences.chinese: 累遷黃門侍郎。
sentences.literal: By stages he was transferred to Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates.
sentences.idiomatic: He rose through several posts to become a gentleman attendant at the palace Yellow Gates.

sentences.chinese: 時吳奮、劉毅俱為侍中，同在門下，雄初不交言。
sentences.literal: At that time Wu Fen and Liu Yi both were palace attendants, together under the gate; at first Xiong did not exchange words.
sentences.idiomatic: Wu Fen and Liu Yi were both palace attendants serving together at court, yet Xiang Xiong still refused to speak to them.

sentences.chinese: 武帝聞之，敕雄令復君臣之好。
sentences.literal: Emperor Wu heard of it and ordered Xiong to restore lord-minister cordiality.
sentences.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu learned of this, he ordered Xiang Xiong to mend relations with his former superiors.

sentences.chinese: 雄不得已，乃詣毅，再拜曰：「向被詔命，君臣義絕，如何？
sentences.literal: Xiong having no choice, then went to Yi, twice bowed and said: Just now having received an edict-order, lord-minister righteousness is cut off—how shall it be?
sentences.idiomatic: Reluctantly Xiang Xiong went to Liu Yi, bowed twice, and said: I have just been commanded to restore cordiality, but the moral bond between lord and minister is already broken—what am I to do?

sentences.chinese: 」於是即去。
sentences.literal: Thereupon at once he departed.
sentences.idiomatic: With that he turned and left.

sentences.chinese: 帝聞而大怒，問雄曰：「我令卿復君臣之好，何以故絕？
sentences.literal: The emperor heard and greatly raged; he asked Xiong: I ordered you to restore lord-minister cordiality—why therefore cut it off?
sentences.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and demanded: I told you to patch things up with your former chief—why did you sever ties instead?

sentences.chinese: 」雄曰：「古之君子進人以禮，退人以禮；
sentences.literal: Xiong said: The gentlemen of antiquity advanced others by ritual and dismissed others by ritual;
sentences.idiomatic: Xiang Xiong answered: Men of virtue in antiquity brought others forward courteously and parted from them courteously;

sentences.chinese: 今之進人若加諸膝，退人若墜諸川。
sentences.literal: those of today who advance others are as placing them on one's knees; those who dismiss others are as dropping them into streams.
sentences.idiomatic: today favorites are lifted onto one's lap, and cast-offs are hurled into the ditch.

sentences.chinese: 劉河內於臣不為戎首，亦已幸甚，安復為君臣之好！
sentences.literal: Liu of Hanoi toward your servant did not act as war-leader—that already is very fortunate; how again lord-minister cordiality!
sentences.idiomatic: Liu Yi did not make himself my mortal enemy as governor of Hanoi; I already count that lucky. How could we pretend to warm lord-and-minister feelings?

sentences.chinese: 」帝從之。
sentences.literal: The emperor followed it.
sentences.idiomatic: The emperor let the matter drop.

sentences.chinese: 泰始中，累遷秦州刺史，假赤幢、曲蓋、鼓吹，賜錢二十萬。
sentences.literal: In the Taishi years, by stages he was transferred to governor of Qinzhou; he was lent crimson canopy, curved umbrella, and drum-and-pipe band; two hundred thousand cash were granted.
sentences.idiomatic: During the Taishi era he advanced to governor of Qin Province, was granted the crimson banner, curved ceremonial canopy, and military musicians, and received a gift of two hundred thousand cash.

sentences.chinese: 咸甯初，入為御史中丞，遷侍中，又出為征虜將軍。
sentences.literal: At the start of Xianning, he entered as imperial secretary vice-director; was transferred to palace attendant; again went out as general who conquers barbarians.
sentences.idiomatic: Early in Xianning he was recalled to serve as vice director of the imperial secretariat, promoted to palace attendant, then sent out again as general for barbarian suppression.

sentences.chinese: 太康初，為河南尹，賜爵關內侯。
sentences.literal: At the start of Taikang, he became Intendant of Henan; a rank of marquis within the passes was granted.
sentences.idiomatic: Early in Taikang he became prefect of the Henan metropolitan district and was ennobled as a secondary marquis.

sentences.chinese: 齊王攸將歸籓，雄諫曰：「陛下子弟雖多，然有名望者少。
sentences.literal: Prince Qi Sima You was about to return to his fief; Xiong remonstrated: Your Majesty's sons and younger brothers though many, yet those with fame and repute are few.
sentences.idiomatic: When Prince Qi, Sima You, was ordered back to his princedom, Xiang Xiong urged against it: You have many imperial clansmen, but few who truly command respect.

sentences.chinese: 齊王臥在京邑，所益實深，不可不思。
sentences.literal: Prince Qi lies at the capital seat; the benefit thereby is truly deep—not possible not to ponder.
sentences.idiomatic: Keeping Prince Qi at the capital does profound good for the realm; you must weigh this carefully.

sentences.chinese: 」帝不納。
sentences.literal: The emperor did not accept.
sentences.idiomatic: The emperor would not heed him.

sentences.chinese: 雄固諫忤旨，起而徑出，遂以憤卒。
sentences.literal: Xiong stubbornly remonstrated and offended intent; he rose and went straight out; thereby in resentment he died.
sentences.idiomatic: Xiang Xiong pressed his advice until he angered the throne, then rose and walked straight out of court; he died soon afterward, consumed by indignation.

sentences.chinese: 弟匡，惠帝世為護軍將軍。
sentences.literal: Younger brother Kuang, in Emperor Hui's age was general who guards the army.
sentences.idiomatic: His younger brother Xiang Kuang became protector-general under Emperor Hui.

sentences.chinese: 段灼，字休然，敦煌人也。
sentences.literal: Duan Zhuo, courtesy Xiuran, was a man of Dunhuang.
sentences.idiomatic: Duan Zhuo, courtesy name Xiuran, was a native of Dunhuang.

sentences.chinese: 世為西土著姓，果直有才辯。
sentences.literal: For generations they were a great surname of the western lands; he was frank and upright and had talent in disputation.
sentences.idiomatic: His family had long been a powerful clan of the northwest; he was blunt, upright, and a gifted debater.

sentences.chinese: 少仕州郡，稍遷鄧艾鎮西司馬，從艾破蜀有功，封關內侯，累遷議郎。
sentences.literal: In youth he served prefectures and commanderies; gradually was promoted Deng Ai's west-guarding army marshal; following Ai he broke Shu with merit; enfeoffed marquis within the passes; by stages transferred to gentleman consultant.
sentences.idiomatic: He entered local administration young, rose to become Deng Ai's chief of staff on the western front, earned distinction in the conquest of Shu, was made a secondary marquis, and eventually reached the post of advisory gentleman.

sentences.chinese: 武帝即位，灼上疏追理艾曰：
sentences.literal: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, Zhuo submitted a memorial pursuing judgment for Ai, saying:
sentences.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu took the throne, Duan Zhuo submitted a memorial arguing for Deng Ai's rehabilitation:

sentences.chinese: 故征西將軍鄧艾，心懷至忠，而荷反逆之名；
sentences.literal: The former general who conquered the west Deng Ai, in heart cherished utmost loyalty, yet bore the name of rebellion;
sentences.idiomatic: The late Deng Ai, former general of the western expedition, was utterly loyal at heart yet was branded a traitor;

sentences.chinese: 平定巴、蜀，而受三族之誅，臣竊悼之。
sentences.literal: he pacified Ba and Shu, yet received execution of three clans; your servant secretly mourns him.
sentences.idiomatic: he conquered Ba and Shu for the court, then suffered the extirpation of three generations of his kin—I mourn him in private.

sentences.chinese: 惜哉，言艾之反也！
sentences.literal: Alas, they speak of Ai's rebellion!
sentences.idiomatic: How regrettable that people still call Deng Ai a rebel!

sentences.chinese: 以艾性剛急，矜功伐善，而不能協同朋類，輕犯雅俗，失君子之心，故莫肯理之。
sentences.literal: Because Ai's nature was rigid and hasty, he boasted of merit and vaunted goodness, yet could not cooperate with peers and companions; lightly he offended refined custom—lost gentlemen's hearts—therefore none were willing to straighten his case.
sentences.idiomatic: Because Deng Ai was blunt and impatient, crowed over his deeds and vaunted his superiority, refused to get along with colleagues, and casually offended respectable opinion, he forfeited the sympathy of good men—so nobody would plead his innocence.

sentences.chinese: 臣敢昧死言艾所以不反之狀。
sentences.literal: Your servant dares, blinding death, to speak the forms by which Ai therefore did not rebel.
sentences.idiomatic: I risk execution to explain why Deng Ai could not have been plotting rebellion.

sentences.chinese: 艾本屯田掌犢人，宣皇帝拔之于農吏之中，顯之於宰府之職。
sentences.literal: Ai originally was a man who managed oxen for agricultural colonies; Emperor Xuan pulled him from among farming clerks and displayed him in steward-office posts.
sentences.idiomatic: Deng Ai began as a lowly clerk overseeing ox teams on the military farms; Emperor Xuan pulled him from that obscurity and advanced him to responsible posts at headquarters.

sentences.chinese: 處內外之官，據文武之任，所在輒有名績，固足以明宣皇帝之知人矣。
sentences.literal: He occupied inner and outer offices, grasped civil and martial duties; wherever posted, always there were famed deeds—solidly sufficient to clarify Emperor Xuan's knowing men.
sentences.idiomatic: Whether at court or in the field, in civil or military roles, he produced a distinguished record everywhere he served—clear proof that Emperor Xuan knew how to spot talent.

sentences.chinese: 會值洮西之役，官兵失利，刺史王經困於圍城之中。
sentences.literal: It happened to meet the Tao-west campaign; court troops suffered defeat; Inspector Wang Jing was trapped within besieged walls.
sentences.idiomatic: Then came the disaster on the Tao River: imperial forces were routed and Inspector Wang Jing was trapped inside a siege.

sentences.chinese: 當爾之時，二州危懼，隴右懍懍，幾非國家之有也。
sentences.literal: At that moment the two provinces were in peril and fear; Longyou trembled—it was almost not the state's possession.
sentences.idiomatic: Both provinces were panic-stricken; the Longyou frontier shook; the region nearly ceased to belong to the state.

sentences.chinese: 先帝以為深憂重慮，思惟可以安邊殺敵莫賢于艾，故授之以兵馬，解狄道之圍。
sentences.literal: The late emperor took it as deep worry and heavy concern; reflecting that none who could pacify the border and kill the enemy surpassed Ai, therefore he entrusted him with troops and horses and relieved Didao's siege.
sentences.idiomatic: The late emperor worried deeply and concluded that no one could secure the frontier and strike the enemy better than Deng Ai, so he gave him an army and lifted the siege of Didao.

sentences.chinese: 圍解，留屯上邽。
sentences.literal: The siege relieved, he remained garrisoned at Shanggui.
sentences.idiomatic: After the siege broke, Deng Ai stayed on to garrison Shanggui.

sentences.chinese: 承官軍大敗之後，士卒破膽，將吏無氣，倉庫空虛，器械殫盡。
sentences.literal: Receiving after court army great defeat, troops broke liver-gall; commanders and clerks without breath; granaries empty and void; weapons exhausted to end.
sentences.idiomatic: Coming right after a shattering defeat, the soldiers were demoralized, officers had no fight left, stores stood empty, and equipment was gone.

sentences.chinese: 艾欲積穀強兵，以待有事。
sentences.literal: Ai wished to pile grain and strengthen troops, to await there being affairs.
sentences.idiomatic: Deng Ai wanted to stockpile grain and rebuild the army against whatever came next.

sentences.chinese: 是歲少雨，又為區種之法，手執耒耜，率先將士，所統萬數，而身不離僕虜之勞，親執士卒之役。
sentences.literal: That year rain was scant; again he practiced pit-field method; hand grasping plough-hoe, he led ahead generals and soldiers; those commanded numbered in myriads, yet his person did not depart labor of servants and captives—personally performed soldiers' corvee.
sentences.idiomatic: Rain was scarce that year, so he introduced pit planting, took hoe and plough in his own hands, and led tens of thousands of troops by example, sharing the dirty work of common soldiers and bondsmen.

sentences.chinese: 故落門、段谷之戰，能以少擊多，摧破強賊，斬首萬計。
sentences.literal: Therefore at Luomen and at Duangu battles, able with few to strike many, he crushed strong bandits; beheaded counted in myriads.
sentences.idiomatic: That is why at Luomen and Duangu he could attack greatly superior forces, shatter powerful enemies, and pile up tens of thousands of counted heads.

sentences.chinese: 遂委艾以廟勝成圖，指授長策。
sentences.literal: Thereupon they entrusted Ai with temple-victory completed plans; pointed and handed long strategies.
sentences.idiomatic: The court then entrusted him with the grand strategy drawn up in council and gave him wide discretionary powers.

sentences.chinese: 艾受命忘身，龍驤麟振，前無堅敵。
sentences.literal: Ai received mandate forgetting self; dragon-soaring, unicorn-shaking—before him no firm foe.
sentences.idiomatic: Deng Ai obeyed orders as if his life meant nothing; he swept forward like a charging dragon or bounding unicorn and met no foe who could stand firm.

sentences.chinese: 蜀地阻險，山高穀深，而艾步乘不滿二萬，束馬懸車，自投死地，勇氣陵雲，將士乘勢，故能使劉禪震怖，君臣面縛。
sentences.literal: Shu terrain was barrier-steep; mountains high, valleys deep; yet Ai's foot and horse did not fill twenty thousand; he bundled horses and suspended carts, himself threw into dead ground; courage overtopped clouds; generals and soldiers rode momentum—therefore able to make Liu Shan tremble in terror; lord and ministers with faces bound.
sentences.idiomatic: Shu was a maze of precipices and deep defiles, yet Deng Ai took fewer than twenty thousand foot and horse, packed horses and hoisted carts over cliffs, and marched into what looked like certain death; courage pierced the clouds, and his men rode that surge until Liu Shan shook with terror and Shu rulers came out bound at their own bidding.

sentences.chinese: 軍不逾時，而巴、蜀蕩定，此艾固足以彰先帝之善任矣。
sentences.literal: The army not exceeding season, yet Ba and Shu were swept settled—this Ai solidly was sufficient to manifest the late emperor's good employment of men.
sentences.idiomatic: In short order Ba and Shu were pacified—clear proof that the late emperor had chosen the right man.

sentences.chinese: 艾功名已成，亦當書之竹帛，傳祚萬世。
sentences.literal: Ai's merit and fame already completed—also ought be written on bamboo and silk; fortune transmitted myriad generations.
sentences.idiomatic: Deng Ai had already secured enduring fame; his deeds belonged on bamboo slips and silk for ten thousand generations.

sentences.chinese: 七十老公，復何所求哉！
sentences.literal: A seventy-year-old man—again what does he seek!
sentences.idiomatic: What more could a man of seventy possibly want?

sentences.chinese: 艾以禪初降，遠郡未附，矯令承制，權安社稷。
sentences.literal: Ai, because Shan had first surrendered, distant commanderies not yet attached, falsely ordered acting under mandate—temporarily to settle altars of soil and grain.
sentences.idiomatic: Because Liu Shan had just surrendered and outlying districts had not yet submitted, Deng Ai issued orders in the emperor's name as an emergency measure to stabilize the state.

sentences.chinese: 雖違常科，有合古義，原心定罪，事可詳論。
sentences.literal: Though it violated constant statutes, it matched ancient meaning; tracing the heart to fix guilt—the affair permits detailed discussion.
sentences.idiomatic: That bent the usual rules but matched ancient precedent; his motives deserve careful weighing before we call it a crime.

sentences.chinese: 故鎮西將軍鐘會，有吞天下之心，恐艾威名，知必不同，因其疑似，構成其事。
sentences.literal: Therefore General Who Guards the West Zhong Hui had a heart to swallow the world; he feared Ai's martial name; knew they surely would not agree—thereupon using his doubtful likeness, he fabricated the affair.
sentences.idiomatic: Zhong Hui, general of the western garrison, dreamed of seizing the empire; he feared Deng Ai's prestige and knew they could never cooperate, so he seized on ambiguous evidence and framed him.

sentences.chinese: 艾被詔書，即遣強兵，束身就縛，不敢顧望。
sentences.literal: Ai received the edict document; at once he sent strong troops; bound body and submitted to bonds—dared not look back.
sentences.idiomatic: When the summons reached him, Deng Ai dismissed his heavy guard, let himself be tied, and never hesitated or looked back.

sentences.chinese: 誠自知奉見先帝，必無當死之理也。
sentences.literal: Truly he himself knew that presenting himself to see the late emperor, surely there was no principle warranting death.
sentences.idiomatic: He believed that once he stood before the late emperor he could not possibly deserve death.

sentences.chinese: 會受誅之後，艾參佐官屬、部曲將吏，愚戇相聚，自共追艾，破壞檻車，解其囚執。
sentences.literal: After Hui received execution, Ai's staff clerks and commanders, foolish and blunt gathered together; themselves together pursued Ai; broke prison cart; released his prisoner bonds.
sentences.idiomatic: After Zhong Hui was executed, Deng Ai's staff officers and unit leaders—simple, stubborn men—rallied, chased down their commander, smashed his cage cart, and freed him from bonds.

sentences.chinese: 艾在困地，是以狼狽失據。
sentences.literal: Ai was in straitened ground; thereby he was wolf-coarse and lost footing.
sentences.idiomatic: Caught in that desperate position, Deng Ai floundered without a foothold.

sentences.chinese: 夫反非小事，若懷噁心，即當謀及豪傑，然後乃能興動大眾，不聞艾有腹心一人。
sentences.literal: Now rebellion is no small matter; if harboring evil mind, then ought plot reaching heroes—afterward then able to rouse great masses; not heard that Ai had one belly-heart man.
sentences.idiomatic: Rebellion is no trifle; a true traitor first wins over bold leaders and only then can stir the masses—yet no one ever named a single confidant of Deng Ai.

sentences.chinese: 臨死口無惡言，獨受腹背之誅，豈不哀哉！
sentences.literal: Facing death mouth had no evil words; alone he received belly-back execution—is it not pitiable!
sentences.idiomatic: He spoke no treason even facing death, yet was destroyed from front and back—is that not heartbreaking?

sentences.chinese: 故見之者垂涕，聞之者歎息。
sentences.literal: Therefore those who saw shed tears; those who heard sighed.
sentences.idiomatic: Witnesses wept; everyone who heard the tale groaned.

sentences.chinese: 此賈誼所以慷慨于漢文，天下之事可為痛哭者，良有以也。
sentences.literal: This is why Jia Yi therefore was impassioned toward Han Wen—affairs under Heaven for which one may bitterly weep—truly there is cause.
sentences.idiomatic: That is why Jia Yi poured out his grief to Emperor Wen of Han: some national wrongs truly merit bitter tears.

sentences.chinese: 陛下龍興，闡弘大度，受誅之家，不拘敘用，聽艾立後，祭祀不絕。
sentences.literal: Your Majesty dragon-rises; spreads vast magnanimity; houses that received execution are not barred from graded employment; allows Ai to establish an heir; sacrifices do not cease.
sentences.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty ascended the dragon throne you have shown magnificent generosity: families that suffered execution are not forever barred from office, and Deng Ai has been allowed an heir so his sacrifices continue.

sentences.chinese: 昔秦人憐白起之無罪，吳人傷子胥之冤酷，皆為之立祠。
sentences.literal: Formerly Qin people pitied Bai Qi's absence of crime; Wu people grieved Zixu's cruel injustice—both for them established shrines.
sentences.idiomatic: The people of Qin mourned Bai Qi as innocent; the people of Wu ached over Wu Zixu's cruel fate—and shrines were raised to both.

sentences.chinese: 天下之人為艾悼心痛恨，亦由是也。
sentences.literal: Under Heaven's people for Ai mourn heart pain hatred—it is also from this.
sentences.idiomatic: The empire's grief and outrage over Deng Ai spring from the same sentiment.

sentences.chinese: 謂可聽艾門生故吏收艾屍柩，歸葬舊墓，還其田宅，以平蜀之功，繼封其後，使艾闔棺定諡，死無所恨。
sentences.literal: I say it is permissible to allow Ai's disciples and former clerks to gather Ai's coffin; return burial to old tomb; restore his fields and houses; by merit of pacifying Shu, continue enfeoffment of his posterity; cause Ai coffin-closed fix posthumous title—dead without regret.
sentences.idiomatic: Let his students and old subordinates recover his remains, bury him in the family plot, restore his lands and houses, ennoble his heirs for the Shu campaign, and settle his posthumous title once the lid is closed—then he can rest without resentment.

sentences.chinese: 赦冤魂于黃泉，收信義於後世，則天下徇名之士，思立功之臣，必投湯火，樂為陛下死矣！
sentences.literal: Pardon wronged souls in yellow springs; gather trust and righteousness in later ages—then under Heaven name-seeking gentlemen, ministers thinking to establish merit, surely will cast into boiling fire, gladly die for Your Majesty!
sentences.idiomatic: Free an unjust ghost in the underworld and win good faith for generations to come, and every reputation-minded gentleman and ambitious commander will rush through fire for Your Majesty!

sentences.chinese: 帝省表，甚嘉其意。
sentences.literal: The emperor examined the memorial; greatly praised its intent.
sentences.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial and warmly approved its spirit.

sentences.chinese: 灼後復陳時宜曰：
sentences.literal: Zhuo afterward again presented timely suitability, saying:
sentences.idiomatic: Later Duan Zhuo submitted further advice on policy of the moment:

sentences.chinese: 臣聞天時不如地利，地利不如人和。
sentences.literal: Your servant has heard: Heaven's timing is not as good as earth's advantage; earth's advantage is not as good as men's harmony.
sentences.idiomatic: I have heard that opportunity from Heaven counts less than terrain, and terrain counts less than unity among the people.

sentences.chinese: 三里之城，五里之郭，圜圍而攻之，有不克者，此天時不如地利。
sentences.literal: A wall three li, an outer wall five li—round-besiege and attack it; there are those not overcome—this is Heaven's timing not as good as earth's advantage.
sentences.idiomatic: Take a tiny citadel ringed by attackers who still cannot crack it—that shows weather and luck lose to strong ground.

sentences.chinese: 城非不高，池非不深，穀非不多，兵非不利，委而去之，此地利不如人和。
sentences.literal: The walls not not high, the moats not not deep, grain not not much, weapons not not sharp—yet cast aside and leave them—this is earth's advantage not as good as men's harmony.
sentences.idiomatic: High walls, deep moats, full granaries, and keen weapons still abandoned mean superior terrain cannot save a divided people.

sentences.chinese: 然古之王者，非不先推恩德，結固人心。
sentences.literal: Yet kings of antiquity were not ones who did not first extend grace and virtue, knotting firm men's hearts.
sentences.idiomatic: Yet true kings of old always began by spreading kindness and binding hearts together.

sentences.chinese: 人心苟和，雖三里之城，五里之郭，不可攻也。
sentences.literal: Men's hearts if harmonious—though a wall three li, outer wall five li—not possible to attack.
sentences.idiomatic: When hearts are united, even a pocket fortress cannot be stormed.

sentences.chinese: 人心不和，雖金城湯池，不能守也。
sentences.literal: Men's hearts if not harmonious—though metal walls, boiling moats—not able to guard.
sentences.idiomatic: When hearts are divided, neither bronze ramparts nor boiling moats will hold.

sentences.chinese: 臣推此以廣其義，舜彈五弦之琴，詠《南風》之詩，而天下自理，由堯人可比屋而封也。
sentences.literal: Your servant pushes this to broaden its meaning: Shun plucked a five-string zither, intoned the poem South Wind, and under Heaven self-ordered—because Yao's people could house-by-house be enfeoffed.
sentences.idiomatic: From this I broaden the point: Shun could rule the realm simply by playing his five-string lute and singing the South Wind ode, because Yao had left the people so virtuous that every household deserved a noble title.

sentences.chinese: 曩者多難，奸雄屢起，攪亂眾心，刀鋸相乘，流死之孤，哀聲未絕。
sentences.literal: Of late many hardships; treacherous heroes repeatedly arose; stirred and disturbed the multitude's hearts; knife and saw succeeded one another; drifting-death orphans—mourning sounds not yet ceased.
sentences.idiomatic: Recent generations have suffered endless turmoil: warlords rose again and again, minds were poisoned, executions followed one after another, and the wailing of refugees has barely faded.

sentences.chinese: 故臣以為陛下當深思遠念，杜漸防萌，彈琴詠詩，垂拱而已。
sentences.literal: Therefore your servant thinks Your Majesty ought deeply think and far ponder; stop gradual, guard sprouts; pluck zither intone poems—hang robe sleeves only.
sentences.idiomatic: So I urge Your Majesty to think deep and far, choke troubles at the bud, and govern chiefly by moral influence rather than constant interference.

sentences.chinese: 其要莫若推恩以協和黎庶，故推恩足以保四海，不推恩不足以保妻子。
sentences.literal: Its essential nothing like extending grace to harmonize black-haired commoners—therefore extending grace suffices to protect four seas; not extending grace does not suffice to protect wife and children.
sentences.idiomatic: Nothing matters more than spreading kindness to unite the common people: generous rule secures the realm; stinginess cannot even protect one's own household.

sentences.chinese: 是故唐堯以親睦九族為先，周文以刑于寡妻為急，明王聖主莫不先親後疏，自近及遠。
sentences.literal: Therefore Tang Yao took intimate harmony of nine kindreds as first; Zhou Wen took model conduct toward few wife as urgent; enlightened kings sagely lords none did not first kin afterward distant, from near reaching far.
sentences.idiomatic: Hence Yao of Tang began by harmonizing his nine clans, King Wen of Zhou by setting an example for his consort; no wise ruler ever neglected kin near at hand before reaching outward.

sentences.chinese: 臣以為太宰、司徒、衛將軍三王宜留洛中鎮守，其餘諸王自州征足任者，年十五以上悉遣之國。
sentences.literal: Your servant thinks Grand Tutor, Minister of Education, Guard General—three kings—ought remain in Luoyang center to guard; the rest of the kings whom provincial evaluation deems fit for duty, age fifteen and above all dispatch them to their states.
sentences.idiomatic: I propose keeping the three princes who hold the posts of grand tutor, minister of education, and guard general in Luoyang to anchor the capital, while every other prince assessed at the provincial level as fit for duty and aged fifteen or older should be sent out to his fief.

sentences.chinese: 為選中郎傅相，才兼文武，以輔佐之。
sentences.literal: For them select central gentleman tutor-ministers, talent spanning civil and martial, to assist them.
sentences.idiomatic: Appoint each a mentor and chief minister chosen from the palace corps, men competent in both civil and military affairs.

sentences.chinese: 聽于其國繕修兵馬，廣布恩信。
sentences.literal: Allow in their states repair troops and horses; broadly spread grace and trust.
sentences.idiomatic: Let them drill troops and spread benevolent authority within their domains.

sentences.chinese: 必撫下猶子，愛國如家，君臣分定，百世不遷，連城開地，為晉、魯、衛。
sentences.literal: Surely they will soothe inferiors like sons; love state like home; lord-minister portions fixed; hundred generations not moved; linked cities open lands—become Jin, Lu, Wei.
sentences.idiomatic: They will cherish subjects like children and the realm like their own household; lord and vassal roles stay fixed for generations; wide domains will stand like the old houses of Jin, Lu, and Wei.

sentences.chinese: 所謂磐石之宗，天下服其強矣。
sentences.literal: What is called clan of rock—under Heaven submits to its strength.
sentences.idiomatic: That is the true rock-solid royal house, and the empire will respect its strength.

sentences.chinese: 雖云割地，譬猶囊漏貯中，亦一家之有耳。
sentences.literal: Though said to divide land, likened still to bag leaking stored within—it is also one family's possession only.
sentences.idiomatic: Granting territory sounds like loss, yet it is wealth shifting inside one purse—it still stays within the imperial clan.

sentences.chinese: 若慮後世強大，自可豫為制度，使得推恩以分子弟。
sentences.literal: If worried posterity strength great, naturally can beforehand make institutions, cause able to extend grace to divide sons and younger brothers.
sentences.idiomatic: If you fear future over-mighty princes, lay down rules now that allow estates to be subdivided among heirs.

sentences.chinese: 如此則枝分葉布，稍自削小，漸使轉至萬國，亦後世之利，非所患也。
sentences.literal: Thus then branches divide leaves spread; gradually self pare small; gradually cause turn arriving myriad states—also posterity's profit; not what is feared.
sentences.idiomatic: Branches will spread and holdings shrink step by step until they resemble the myriad states of old—a benefit to later reigns, not a danger.

sentences.chinese: 昔在漢世，諸呂自疑，內有硃虛、東牟之親，外有諸侯九國之強，故不敢動搖。
sentences.literal: Formerly in Han age, various Lü self-doubt; inside had Zhu Xu, Dong Mou kin; outside had feudal lords nine states' strength—therefore dared not shake move.
sentences.idiomatic: Under Han the Lü clan hesitated because inside court stood princes like Liu Zhang of Zhu Xu and Liu Xingju of Dong Mou, while outside nine powerful kingdoms watched—so they dared not strike.

sentences.chinese: 於今之宜，諸侯強大，是為太山之固。
sentences.literal: As for today's suitability, feudal lords strong great—this makes Mount Tai's firmness.
sentences.idiomatic: For present needs, strong regional princes are the surest bulwark—solid as Mount Tai.

sentences.chinese: 非我族類，其心必異。
sentences.literal: Not our clan kind—their hearts surely different.
sentences.idiomatic: Those outside the royal kin will never share the same loyalty.

sentences.chinese: 而魏法禁錮諸王，親戚隔絕，不祥莫大焉。
sentences.literal: Yet Wei law imprisoned fetters various kings; kin and affines cut off—no ill omen greater than this.
sentences.idiomatic: Yet Wei law penned princes like criminals and severed family ties—nothing could be more ominous.

sentences.chinese: 間者無故又瓜分天下，立五等諸侯。
sentences.literal: Recently without cause again melon-divided under Heaven, establishing five-ranks feudal lords.
sentences.idiomatic: Lately the realm has again been carved into feudal allotments for no compelling reason, reviving the five-grade nobility.
